cashComposition.title: Cash composition
cashComposition.content:
The combined Cash & equivalents line above is the financial-parser's own definition choice: narrow cash and bank balances plus term deposits held at banks. This chart splits the two.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: term deposits are the larger piece in most periods (e.g. CNY1,100.5m of term deposits vs CNY503.3m cash-only at FY2025) -- a pre-revenue/early-commercial biotech parking a clinical-trial-funding war chest in short-dated deposits rather than leaving it all in demand accounts.

What to watch:

  • Term deposits shrinking faster than cash-only as trial and launch spend accelerates -- the runway question
  • A shift back toward cash-only ahead of a known cash need (debt maturity, milestone payment)

niNci.title: Net income: attributable vs including NCI
niNci.content:
Net income (attributable) is the owners'-share profit used everywhere else on this dashboard and in the DCF. Net income incl. NCI is the consolidated figure before non-controlling interests' share is carved out.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the two lines track closely here -- unlike a holding company with a large minority-owned subsidiary, Keymed's NCI slice is small, so this chart is mainly a check that it stays small rather than a story in its own right.

What to watch:

  • A widening gap signalling a consolidated subsidiary with a growing minority stake
  • Either line swinging to loss while the other stays positive, which would flag the NCI share moving opposite to the group

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Keymed Biosciences Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
